title: Reaching Out to Professors: Why It Actually Matters
excerpt: Contacting professors isn't only for PhD applications. Here's why you might need to reach out and in what scenarios it really helps.

blocks.text: The topic of connecting with professors abroad and maybe also inside the country. In this part we want to talk about how to connect with professors and divide it into several parts. First, why this connection matters and in what use cases we need this connection. Second, how we find professors related to our own field of work. By field of work I mean the same academic field, so to speak. And third, what we even say to them and how we connect. We're going to answer these three, then. First let's get to the why, the reason for this work.
Many times it happens that you need to connect with professors abroad in different scenarios.
For example, one of them is about applying for a PhD.
Another one of the use cases we have is inviting professors to work on papers. For example, you want to work on a joint paper with each other.

Another one of the use cases that exists is getting, for example, the code or dataset of a paper. For example, you liked a paper, you want to connect with the authors of that paper and have them send you the dataset of that paper or send you its benchmark or even send you its code. In these scenarios, connecting is really necessary and you'll need it.
So don't only think that connecting with professors abroad or inside the country is necessarily for a PhD. No, it has different scenarios.

For example, I remember back when I wanted to choose the topic of my master's proposal, I messaged many researchers around the world and many professors around the world and asked them, for example, if possible to spare an hour for me, or for example to suggest to me an up-to-date topic that they know about and are working on, and many of them answered.

Of course these answers might be somewhere the person says I'm busy and can't manage, or many also answered me and introduced the topic of the field that it was, and well I really got ideas from these same ones.

So in the first part of this text and this folder, I basically want us to answer these why's and always keep these why's in our mind and go at this issue with an open view and not always limit this connection to getting, for example, a PhD offer.
